one_liner: SQL/HTTP full-text and analytics search database, C++ core, positioned as a faster Elasticsearch alternative.
what_it_does: Manticore Search is a standalone search/analytics database daemon that indexes text, numeric, and vector data and serves queries over MySQL-wire SQL and an HTTP JSON API. It targets the same use cases as Elasticsearch (full-text search, log analytics, faceting, KNN/hybrid search) but with SQL as the native query language instead of a JSON Query DSL. It is a server you deploy (package, Docker, or source build), not an embeddable library.
how_it_is_fast: Query execution is multi-threaded across all CPU cores with a cost-based optimizer choosing execution plans from indexed-data statistics. It offers both row-wise storage (faster, more RAM) and a separate columnar storage engine (Manticore Columnar Library) for datasets too large for RAM. Automatic secondary indexes use a PGM-index (Piecewise Geometric Model) for key-to-location mapping instead of classic B-trees. The core inverted-index/search engine descends from the Sphinx search engine, rewritten and extended in C++17.
when_to_use: Log/analytics workloads (e.g. nginx logs, time-series) where columnar storage plus the cost-based optimizer avoid JVM/Lucene overhead
Teams that want SQL over full-text/analytics search rather than learning Elasticsearch's Query DSL, especially existing MySQL-protocol tooling
Ingest-heavy pipelines where bulk-load throughput matters more than incremental refresh latency
Resource-constrained deployments: README states ~40MB RSS for an empty instance
Single query needing both full-text and vector/KNN retrieval (hybrid search) without a separate vector DB
when_not_to_use: Need Elasticsearch's mature aggregation framework, Query DSL, or its large ecosystem of plugins/native Kibana support
Can't accept GPL-3.0 copyleft for embedding into proprietary systems (vs Elasticsearch's SSPL/Elastic license)
Require strict ACID guarantees: README states Manticore is 'not fully ACID-compliant', offering only isolated transactions and binary logging

Basing a purchase decision on the cited speedup numbers: the db-benchmarks.com suite behind them is maintained by the same Manticore team, so treat 4x/15x/22x/25x/2x figures as vendor-reported, not independent
Need multi-master replication stronger than Galera-based 'virtually synchronous' replication provides

integration.dependencies: Bundled Manticore Columnar Library (git submodule) for columnar storage; optional ICU for CJK/Chinese segmentation; various vendored libs under .gitmodules. Not a linkable library — ships as searchd/indexer binaries.
integration.platforms: Linux (Debian/Ubuntu, RHEL/CentOS/Amazon/Oracle/Fedora families) and macOS via Homebrew per install script; Windows has its own CI test template (win_test_template.yml). x86-64 assumed; ARM support not documented in README.
integration.thread_safety: not documented as a library API (there is none); server internally runs multi-threaded query execution and parallelizes across cores per README
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: has an Elasticsearch-compatible HTTP write path and MySQL-protocol SQL access, so ingestion pipelines (Logstash/Filebeat/Kafka) can be repointed, but query code must be rewritten from Elasticsearch's Query DSL to Manticore SQL or its own HTTP JSON search syntax.

gotchas: README explicitly states Manticore is 'not fully ACID-compliant' despite having isolated transactions and binlog
Columnar storage saves RAM but README says it gives 'lower performance than row-wise storage for some kinds of queries' — pick per-table
GPL-3.0 licensed and historically forked from the Sphinx search engine — copyleft terms differ materially from Elasticsearch's license

The benchmark suite (db-benchmarks.com / github.com/db-benchmarks/db-benchmarks) used for the headline multipliers is run by the same Manticore team (top contributor sanikolaev), not an independent third party
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The sibling entries are either embeddable Lucene-replacement indexing libraries (IResearch, Tantivy, SeekStorm) or single-machine grep-replacement CLIs (frg, ngi, trigrep, ugrep); Manticore is the only full standalone SQL/HTTP search server in the set. Pick it when you need a deployable, replicated, multi-user database with backup/restore and SQL access rather than a library to embed in your own indexing pipeline, and specifically over Elasticsearch when your workload matches log/analytics/full-text patterns and you can accept GPL-3.0 and a smaller ecosystem.
verified_claims_summary: Vendor blog (Manticore, Jul 2022) benchmarked Manticore 5.0.0-5.0.2 against Elasticsearch 7.15.2/8.3.2 on a 32-core SSD server (CPU model and compiler flags unstated): 4x faster on a 1.7B-row taxi dataset, 15x on 1.1M Hacker News comments, 22x on 10M nginx log lines, 25x faster bulk-load of the 1.7B-doc set (1h08m vs 28h33m via Logstash), and roughly 2x higher direct-load throughput for 50M docs (894,856 vs 416,788 docs/s, sharded configs) — though unsharded default Elasticsearch was actually 21% faster in that same test. The db-benchmarks.com suite behind these numbers is maintained by the Manticore team itself.
status_note: Actively maintained (record's last_commit is current, large nightly/CI test matrix in .github/workflows) and free to install via package manager, Docker, or source build; GPL-3.0 licensing is the main friction point for proprietary embedding rather than any maturity concern.
